verse: "Be still and know that I am God; I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted over the earth."
story: Earthquake, roaring seas and raging nations fill this psalm, and then, in the middle of the noise, God Himself speaks.

The command to be still is not advice to relax. The Hebrew sense is closer to let go, drop your hands, stop striving. It is spoken to nations and to anxious hearts alike. The reason follows at once: He is God, and He will be exalted over the earth. The world's turmoil does not decide the outcome, and neither do our plans. The city of God is glad because God is in the midst of it, and that presence is unshaken. Christ is that presence with us.
Set your hands down for a minute today. Let Him be God over the thing you are gripping.
